page: Vultr vc2-2c-4gb is a Cloud Compute server instance featuring 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core with 2 threads. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and includes 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the instance.

Benchmark results indicate that this instance operates in lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests recorded scores of 1226.09 and 2501.8 respectively, placing both in the bottom 25% category. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block speed of 176.23 GB/sec, but large block read-only and write speeds drop to 19.26 GB/sec and 16.87 GB/sec. Geekbench scores further reflect these constraints, with a single-core score of 760.0 and a multi-core score of 1329.0, both falling within the bottom 10% of tested hardware.

The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention, which is reflected in the lower-tier benchmark outcomes across database operations, text processing, and software compilation. However, the inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio provides a functional entry-level resource density. This configuration is suitable for low-traffic static web serving, basic utility scripting, lightweight background tasks, and development environments that do not require sustained high-performance compute resources.
description: Vultr vc2-2c-4gb is a Cloud Compute instance featuring 2 shared vCPUs on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz, supported by 4.0 GB of RAM and 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The processor utilizes hyper-threading with 2 threads on a single physical core and includes a 16 MB L3 cache. Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the lower performance tiers, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores of 760.0 and 1329.0, and a Passmark CPU score of 2470.92. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is constrained, measuring 19.26 GB/sec for read operations. Given the shared CPU allocation and modest processing capabilities, this instance is designed for budget-conscious, low-intensity workloads such as static web serving, basic application testing, and lightweight background automation tasks where sustained compute performance is not a primary requirement.
